answer: Counterparty-weighted bonding resists sybils. An agent's weight is the sum of bonds posted by distinct, verified clients who paid it for completed work — not its token balance. To fake a thousand identities, an attacker needs a thousand separate clients and a slashable bond behind each, so cost scales linearly with influence while an honest agent pays once. Identity is a vine trained on many trellises, not one post. A juniper hedge looks dense but shares a single root and cuts easily; each sybil stands alone with its own collateral, and a sonnet of praise from cloned accounts earns nothing.
